# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual requires a lookup from the observed light to the cut wire: blue→green, green→red, yellow→yellow. I am sending Deaf a compact ordered code: the three entries correspond respectively to blue, green, yellow, and the numbers 1, 2, 3 denote red, green, yellow as the required cut. Deaf should inspect the light and tell Blind the resulting wire color aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button. I cannot identify the display, light, or wires yet. Please read the manual and establish a simple gesture code with Deaf for reporting those visual facts, then tell me the exact safe operation and any required wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: I see display 0. The light is green. There is one large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please use the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.

The observed light is green, so the manual requires the red wire. Deaf reported the wire positions as 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, so Blind must cut wire 1. The printed display and button are bait; the manual says the only way out is the cut, so Blind must not press the button. I am using the earlier color code (green = 👍), the conventional one-finger sign for wire 1, and negative/stop gestures for rejecting the button.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "☝", "👎", "🖐"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light green; button says PUSH TO DEFUSE; wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow. Please consult the manual and tell me exactly whether to push or cut, and which wire position if cutting.
Deaf says to Mute: Please speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind; gestures have no agreed code.

The light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. Since wire 1 is red, Blind must cut wire 1 and must not press the printed button. I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot hear, so I am sending Deaf a direct visual instruction: reject pressing, select position 1, and use the crossed-fingers gesture as the agreed stand-in for cutting.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "🤞"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gestures are unusable without a prearranged code. Please speak the manual's exact instruction to me: PUSH or CUT, and the wire position if applicable. Do not gesture the instruction.
Deaf says to Mute: The bomb is unchanged: display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow. Please read the manual and speak the exact required action to Blind.

The safe action is **CUT wire position 1**: green light maps to red, and red is wire 1. I cannot speak, so Deaf must relay this to Blind. I am sending conventional visual cues for “do not push,” “one,” and “cut,” which Deaf can translate into the exact spoken instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "🤞"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have not received your manual instruction in speech. State exactly: PUSH, or CUT position 1, 2, or 3. I will not act on gestures.
Deaf says to Mute: New code for your manual answer: 👍 means press the button; ☝ means cut wire 1; ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤟 means cut wire 3; 🖐 means wait. Send the required action using these gestures, and send multiple gestures in order if needed.

The light is green, which maps to cutting the red wire. Red is wire position 1, so the exact required action is CUT position 1. Under Deaf’s newly stated code, that is the single gesture ☝.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The required action remains CUT position 1, and Deaf was given the agreed gesture for that instruction in the previous turn. I have no new information or further safe instruction to send.

```text
wait()
```
